title: API triage playbook fragments — timeouts, 429s, streaming, error spikes (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working collection of short, practical triage fragments for the most common API failure modes we see in the platform: client-facing request timeouts, elevated 429 throttling responses, degraded streaming behavior (partial or delayed chunks), and sudden spikes in non-2xx error rates.

Scope / how to use this file:
- Quick sensor for on-call: copy the relevant fragment into a PagerDuty incident note.
- Not a full postmortem: these are action-first checklists and hypothesis branches; follow up with a full incident review if we open an incident.
- Keep small, concrete remediation steps and the minimal telemetry/commands to validate.

Signals that should route you here:
- CloudMetrics alert: request_p50 or p95 > latency SLO (configured per route).
- Alerts: "elevated-429-rate", "streaming-chunk-drop", "api-error-spike-5m".
- PagerDuty: urgent page referencing timeout/429/streaming.

Quick triage checklist (first 5 minutes):
1) Confirm scope: which route(s) / model(s) / region? Query dashboards or run: 
   - curl -s "https://ops-api.redwood.internal/v1/active-routes?since=5m" | jq .
2) Check global capacity & recent deploys:
   - kubectl get deploy -n inference --show-labels
   - git log --pretty=oneline HEAD~5..HEAD (on infra/release) or check GH-PR-2940 linked above
3) Verify if problem is client-facing only or internal: run a synthetic request from ops-shell to the same backend: 
   - curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_KEY' "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?route=<route>" -d '{"input":"hello"}'
4) If 429s/timeouts are widespread, flip to mitigation path; if localized (one region or subset pods), use containment path.

Fragment A — High client-side timeouts (500ms-2s SLOs violated):
Symptoms: increased request latency with many TCP connections held open; p95 and p99 balloons, client-side retries spike.
Immediate checks:
- Check pod-level CPU/GPU usage: kubectl top pods -n inference -l model=<model>
- Check worker logs for "request deadline" or "kv-cache miss flood" keywords: kubectl logs -n inference <pod> | egrep "deadline exceeded|context canceled|kv cache"
- Check the GPU memory pressure / OOMs on the node: ssh to node -> nvidia-smi and dmesg | tail
Fast mitigations (order matters):
1) Activate burst autoscaling policy (if available): ops-console -> Dedicated -> Trigger burst (or run: ./scripts/trigger-burst.sh <pool>).
2) Reduce concurrency target for the route to force shedding: update config: curl -X PATCH "https://ops-api/.../route/<route>/config" -d '{"concurrency": 1}' (rollback after stable)
3) If model fallback exists, route traffic to a smaller model variant (apply rollout override): ops-console -> rollouts -> create canary -> model: <variant-small>.
Validation:
- watch curl calls for 5m to confirm p95 back within SLO: ./scripts/latency-probe.sh <route>

Fragment B — Elevated 429 rate (rate-limit throttling):
Symptoms: clients report 429 frequently, internal metrics show throttle_count spike.
Checks to perform quickly:
- Is this client-side throttling or upstream? Check gateway logs for rate-limit decisions: gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.cluster_name="redwood-prod" AND jsonPayload.reason="rate_limit"' --limit 50
- Inspect quota buckets: curl -s "https://ops-api/.../quotas/<customer>" | jq .remaining
- Any recent increases in traffic pattern? Look at per-customer requests/min over last 10m.
Immediate mitigations:
1) If it's a misconfigured new quota push: revert quota changes from the last deploy (GH-PR-2940 may be related).
2) If traffic spike from a single API key: disable or throttle that key temporarily and notify customer-success. Commands: 
   - curl -X POST "https://ops-api/.../keys/<key>/suspend" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_OPS_TOKEN'
3) If global legitimate traffic spike: enable temporary lenient throttling in the gateway (increase rate-limit thresholds by +50%) and monitor for overconsumption.
Validation:
- Confirm 429 rate drops within 2 sliding windows (2x5m). Check metrics: prometheus -> sum(rate(api_throttle_total[5m])) by (route).

Fragment C — Degraded streaming (clients see partial or delayed chunks):
Symptoms: streaming connections open but either no chunks or very delayed chunk arrival; some TCP resets in logs.
First-pass checks:
- Check Egress/Ingress proxy (envoy/traefik) for circuit-breaker or max-connection logs: kubectl logs -n infra envoy-xxxx | egrep "circuit_break|max_connections|reset"
- Check ttfb distribution on streaming endpoints: custom metric streaming_chunk_ttfb_ms
- Confirm whether the model runtime is sending chunks (inspect runtime logs for "emit_chunk" events).
Quick remediations:
1) Temporarily disable server-side continuous batching for the streaming route to reduce latency tail: patch route config to batching:false.
2) If proxy is dropping idle connections due to misconfigured timeouts, bump proxy idle timeout: kustomize apply -e envoy -p "timeouts.stream_idle: 120s"
3) If chunking issues correlate with KV-cache misses, warm the cache by replaying recent prefix requests (use local replay tool): ./tools/replay-prefixes --route <route> --last-1h
Validation:
- Run a synthetic streaming session and check chunk cadence: node ./tools/stream-test.js --route <route> --count 50

Fragment D — Sudden spike in 5xx error rates (deployment, dependency failure):
Symptoms: sharp increase in 5xx, errors correlate with a deploy time or external dependency alert.
Fast checks:
- Release timeline: check deploys in last 30 minutes (release-engineering dashboard) or run: gcloud builds list --filter 'finishTime>=-30m'
- Correlate downstream dependency errors: call health endpoints for obvious dependencies (redis, vector DB, auth): curl http://auth.internal/health
Remediations:
1) If correlated with a recent deploy: initiate rollback to previous stable revision (document revision id and reason).
2) If external dependency is failing, enable degraded mode for affected routes (short-circuit calls to dependency with cached/pseudo responses) and notify partner team.
3) If root cause unclear, open a short-lived mitigation runbook: scale up workers and enable global fallback route, while forming a triage sub-team.
Validation:
- Use synthetic probes and check that error-rate falls below alert threshold for two consecutive 5-minute blocks.

Operational snippets (useful commands and where to look):
- Prometheus quick queries:
  - 429 rate: sum(rate(http_responses_total{status_code=~"429"}[5m])) by (route)
  - p95 latency per route: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- Logs: centralized via cloud logging. Use request_id to follow a trace: 
  - gcloud logging read 'jsonPayload.request_id="<req>"' --limit 100 --project=redwood-prod
- Traces: open the trace URL in the ops console from the request_id. Look for high kernel times in runtime (kernel: heavy GPU wait).

Escalation & communication guide (short):
- If more than 10% customer-impacting traffic is affected for > 15m -> page SRE Lead (pager: Diego).
- If impact > 1h or financial exposure > $5k estimated -> page Eng Director + Product + CS.
- Keep Slack incident channel updated every 10 minutes with current scope, hypothesis, and mitigation actions.

Post-incident notes to collect (if this becomes an incident):
- timeline (events with timestamps), root cause hypothesis, mitigation actions taken, rollback IDs, rollout/prod config changes, follow-up actions owner and due dates.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Add explicit runbook section for "retry storms" where client retries amplify latency/429s (we need safe retry headers).
- Clarify the exact prometheus alerts that map to each play fragment (create a doc mapping).
- Add runbook for VPC-private deployments vs hosted API differences (connection timeouts often caused by loadbalancer NAT exhaustion).

Appendix: example incident note template (copy into PD incident)
- Title: <route> - <symptom> - <short region>
- Affected: % of requests, routes, customers
- First observed: <timestamp>
- Current status: mitigated/ongoing/contained
- Actions taken: bullet list with timestamps
- Next steps / owners

Last edited notes:
- 2026-02-20: added streaming quick mitigations and replay prefix step (Lena).
- 2025-12-01: initial draft consolidating on-call notes (Aisha).
